# Suites excluded from the Linux CI gate. Currently EMPTY, deliberately.
#
# The gate covers every discovered `*.test.ts`. Nothing is skipped, so a green `typescript` job means
# the whole TypeScript suite passed rather than the part somebody chose. Measured in run 30303366777:
# `Ran 1193 tests across 55 files. [359.69s]`, 1192 pass / 0 fail, and the partition check confirmed
# `55 suites executed, exactly the 55 gated, none of the 0 quarantined`.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS EMPTY, rather than not existing:
#
# It was created with three entries, taken from the record in
# src/__tests__/helpers/source-assertions.ts, which stated that three suites were "PERMANENTLY RED on
# Linux" for environmental reasons — measured 3 of 3 runs on `main` at 40c37b1. The first CI run this
# repository has ever had (run 30302342895) then re-ran all three on a GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04
# runner and every one of them passed:
#
#   src/__tests__/config.test.ts                          44 pass /  0 fail    (   0.10s)
#   src/__tests__/macos-app-lifecycle.test.ts            140 pass /  0 fail    ( 358.85s)
#   src/__tests__/native-app-companion-contract.test.ts   14 pass /  0 fail    (   4.50s)
#
# So "permanently red on Linux" was never a property of Linux. It is a property of the STATION: that
# box routinely runs several full recordings suites at once out of different worktrees, and this
# suite scans a shared /tmp, so the suites corrupt each other's fixtures — which is exactly what
# source-assertions.ts warns about two paragraphs above the list. The 92 failures in
# macos-app-lifecycle were FIFO synchronisation timeouts under that contention, not defects.
#
# That is why the mechanism is kept with an empty list instead of being deleted. It is the only
# reason the three entries were ever disproven: `scripts/ci-linux-suite.ts` re-runs each quarantined
# suite and FAILS when one passes, so the exemptions invalidated themselves on their first run
# against a clean machine. A quarantine without that property is where suites go to be forgotten.
#
# TO ADD AN ENTRY: one repo-relative path per line, directly under a line of the form
#
#     # reason: <why this suite cannot pass in CI>
#
# Both halves are enforced by `bun run verify:ci-suite` — an entry naming a suite that does not
# exist fails, and so does an entry without its own `# reason:` line immediately above it. The
# marker is required rather than any comment because the prose above would otherwise satisfy the
# check for whatever entry got appended to it first.
#
# And measure on a QUIET machine, or in CI, before you add anything: the record this file replaced
# was produced on a contended one and named three suites that were never actually broken.
